items.title: Нативный аккордеон
items.description: Аккордеон на нативных details и summary: раскрытие без единой строки JS, ни рамок, ни плашки — список живёт прямо на фоне страницы.
items.docs: Компонент самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей, собственная палитра в локальных переменных --vibeui-accordion-001-*. Раскрытие держат нативные <details>/<summary>, поэтому состояние работает до гидратации и не требует React. Взаимное исключение включается атрибутом name у details. Тема берётся из color-scheme окружения через light-dark(): фона у компонента по умолчанию нет, он лежит прямо на фоне страницы и темнеет вместе с ней. Значок выбирается пропом marker и рисуется самим компонентом в боксе постоянного размера, поэтому текст начинается на одном месте при любой фигуре и картинка одинакова во всех браузерах. Отступы и кегль считаются от собственной ширины через @container.

ai.summary: Аккордеон без JS: раскрытие держат нативные details и summary, а взаимное исключение — атрибут name на details. Дизайн держится на типографике, вертикальном ритме и линии под открытым заголовком: ни рамки, ни плашки, ни фона у строк. Тема приходит из color-scheme окружения через light-dark(), собственного фона у компонента нет. Ноль зависимостей, один файл.

en.description: An accordion built on native details and summary: it opens without a line of JS, and with no border or panel of its own the list sits straight on the page background.

ai.summary: A JS-free accordion: native details and summary handle opening, and the name attribute on details makes the sections exclusive. Keyboard support, find-on-page (the browser opens the matching section) and pre-hydration behaviour all come for free. The design rests on typography, vertical rhythm and the rule under an open heading: no border, no panel, no row fills. The theme comes from the surrounding color-scheme through light-dark(), and the component carries no background of its own. Zero dependencies, one file.

the name attribute on details — that is the exclusivity, no separate state is needed for it

the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself
the fixed 0.625rem marker box: the answer indent is measured from it, so the text does not shift when marker changes
the rule under an open heading as a shadow rather than a border: a border would add height to the row

the @container query instead of a media query: the accordion lives both in a narrow column and full width

The system ::marker is hidden on purpose: every engine draws it differently, so Chrome, Firefox and Safari would not match. The component draws the marker itself.
The name attribute on details is supported by current browsers; older ones simply leave the sections independent, which does not break the component.
Do not animate the open height by hand: native details has no such animation, and faking it brings back the JS this component exists to avoid.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the component has to stay a single file.

en.title: Native Accordion

items.question: What exactly do I get after installing?
items.answer: One component file in your project. The very same one you saw in the preview: no build step, no wrappers, no tie to our theme.

items.question: What if I already have a design system?
items.answer: The component carries its own palette in local variables. Override them and it fits your theme without touching the rest of the project.

items.question: Do I need to install extra libraries?
items.answer: No. Every component declares its dependencies in metadata, and most have none at all: just React.

en.description: An accordion of separate cards: every section has its own border, and the open one sets itself apart with a lift, a ring or just its border — your pick.

ai.summary: An accordion where each section is a card in its own right rather than a row in one sheet. The cards have no fill: they sit on the page background and are held by their border alone. Native details and summary do the opening, so keyboard support, find-on-page and pre-hydration state work without JS. The open card sets itself apart — lifted, held in a ring, or marked by its border alone: that is the elevation prop. Sections are independent; the name attribute is deliberately absent. The theme comes from the surrounding color-scheme through light-dark(). Zero dependencies, one file.

en.title: Card Accordion

items.question: How does billing work?
items.answer: Monthly or yearly. A year costs two months less, the invoice is issued up front, and you can cancel at any point — we refund the remainder pro rata.

items.question: Is my data safe?
items.answer: Encryption in transit and at rest, daily backups kept for 30 days, role-based access. Keys are stored apart from the data.

items.question: Which integrations are supported?
items.answer: Ready-made links to mail, payments and analytics. Everything else goes through webhooks and an open API; keys are issued in the project settings.

items.title: Аккордеон в две колонки
items.description: Аккордеон в две колонки: на широкой раскладке вопрос остаётся слева, а ответ раскрывается справа — глаз не теряет вопрос под длинным текстом.
items.docs: Компонент самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей, собственная палитра в локальных переменных --vibeui-accordion-010-*. Раскрытие держат нативные <details>/<summary>. Две колонки включает @container по ширине самого блока, а не окна: в узкой колонке он сам складывается в обычный список, где бы ни стоял. Фона нет, тема берётся из color-scheme окружения через light-dark(). Отступы и кегль считаются от собственной ширины.

en.description: A two-column accordion: on a wide layout the question stays on the left while the answer opens on the right, so the eye never loses the question under a long answer.

ai.summary: A two-column accordion: on a wide layout the question stays on the left while the answer opens on the right — the row does not break vertically, and the eye never loses the question under a long answer. In a narrow column the block folds into an ordinary list on its own: the layout is decided by @container against the block's width, not by a media query against the window. Native details and summary do the opening, with no JS. There is no background, and the theme comes from the surrounding color-scheme through light-dark(). Zero dependencies, one file.
preserve: the local --vibeui-accordion-010-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-card, border-border and the like)
the native details/summary: replacing them with buttons and useState gives up find-on-page, keyboard behaviour and pre-hydration state

@container against the block width rather than a media query against the window: next to a sidebar the window is wider than the space available, and a media query would open two columns where there is no room for them
folding into one column on a narrow layout: two columns of 20em each are unreadable
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background
numbering as its own prop rather than part of the heading: people cite a question by its number in an email
the fixed marker box: the content indent is measured from it, so rows do not jump when marker changes
the focus-visible outline on summary: headings are tabbed through
the @container query instead of a media query: the component lives both in a narrow column and full width
the <style> block inside the component — it holds the palette, the layout and the marker
adapt: the items array: questions and answers
marker — the section marker: chevron, triangle, square, plus or none
numbered — number the questions
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
defaultOpen — which question starts open; -1 closes them all
the accent through the accent prop — it colours the number, the marker and the focus ring
max width and outer spacing through className
notes: The theme comes from color-scheme. For the component to darken with the system, the project must declare color-scheme: light dark on html — otherwise light-dark() always returns the light branch.
The component needs width: in a column narrower than 32em it is always single-row, and it then offers nothing over accordion-003.
Keep questions to one or two lines. A four-line question fills the left column and pushes the answer to the bottom.
Do not animate the open height by hand: native details has no such animation, and faking it brings back the JS this component exists to avoid.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the component has to stay a single file.

  ]}

en.title: Split Accordion

items.question: How is this different from an ordinary component library?
items.answer: A library gives you a package that lives in node_modules and updates along with the rest of the project. Here the component arrives as a single file and becomes yours: you can edit it, rename it and publish it with your site. In exchange it does not update itself — a new version is installed by the same command.

items.question: Why does each component carry its own palette instead of theme tokens?
items.answer: A component has to look in your project exactly as it did in the preview, and everyone's tokens differ: bg-primary is blue in one project and black in another. Local --vibeui-* variables give a predictable look straight away and still let you override the colours in one line when you need to.

items.question: What exactly does an AI agent get from the Copy for AI link?
items.answer: A text instruction: the component identifier, the install command, the file address, and the lists of what must not change and what may. The agent downloads the file from the registry instead of inventing a lookalike from a description — that is what the instruction exists for.

items.name: accordion-011
items.title: Тёмный аккордеон
items.description: Тёмный аккордеон для тёмных секций: собственная тёмная палитра, а не инверсия светлой. Открытый раздел светится изнутри — тени на тёмном фоне не работают.
items.docs: Компонент самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей, собственная палитра в локальных переменных --vibeui-accordion-011-*. В отличие от остальных аккордеонов семейства он не следует color-scheme окружения: у него собственная тёмная палитра, и она не меняется. Светлый аккордеон на тёмной секции выглядит вырезанной наклейкой, поэтому здесь тёмный вариант, а не инверсия готового. Открытый раздел подсвечивается изнутри — тени на тёмном фоне не работают, и чем именно подсвечивать, решает проп glow. Раскрытие держат нативные <details>/<summary>, взаимное исключение — атрибут name. Отступы и кегль считаются от собственной ширины через @container.

ai.usage:
<Accordion011
  marker="chevron"
  glow="edge"
  items={[
    { question: "Подойдёт для тёмной секции?", answer: "Да, у него своя тёмная палитра." },
  ]}
/>
ai.summary: Тёмный аккордеон для тёмных секций страницы: у него собственная тёмная палитра, а не инверсия светлой. Он единственный в семействе, кто не следует теме окружения, — это и есть его смысл: его ставят туда, где секция тёмная всегда. Открытый раздел подсвечивается изнутри градиентом от края или кольцом, потому что тени на тёмном фоне не читаются. Раскрытие держат нативные details и summary, взаимное исключение — атрибут name. Ноль зависимостей, один файл.

en.description: A dark accordion for dark sections: a palette built dark rather than an inverted light one. The open section glows from within — shadows do not work on a dark ground.

ai.summary: A dark accordion for dark sections: it carries a dark palette of its own rather than an inversion of a light one. It is the only one in the family that does not follow the surrounding theme — that is the whole point: you place it where the section is dark for good. The open section is lit from within by a gradient from its edge or by a ring, because shadows do not read on a dark ground. Native details and summary do the opening, and the name attribute makes the sections exclusive. Zero dependencies, one file.

lighting the open section instead of shadowing it: a shadow does not read on a dark ground in any variant
the name attribute on details — that is the exclusivity, no separate state is needed for it
the round pad behind the marker: on a dark ground a thin edge is lost without it
the fixed marker box: the content indent is measured from it, so rows do not jump when marker changes
the focus-visible outline on summary: headings are tabbed through

marker — the shape in the circle: chevron, triangle, square, plus or none

defaultOpen — which section starts open; -1 closes them all

the accent through the accent prop — it colours the glow, the marker and the focus ring

notes: The component is always dark and does not watch color-scheme. On a light page it will be a dark rectangle — that is expected: for a light section take accordion-001 or accordion-002, which follow the surrounding theme.

glow="none" leaves the open section distinguished by its fill alone — check that the difference is visible against your section background.
Do not animate the open height by hand: native details has no such animation, and faking it brings back the JS this component exists to avoid.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the component has to stay a single file.

en.title: Dark Accordion

items.question: Will this suit a dark section?
items.answer: This one will: it has a dark palette of its own rather than an inversion of a light one. A light accordion on a dark ground reads as a sticker cut out and pasted on, which is why there are two variants and you pick the one that matches the section.

items.question: How do I recolour it for my brand?
items.answer: Through the accent prop or by overriding the local variables. The rest of the palette is built around the accent, so one value is enough.

items.question: Why is the open section lit rather than shadowed?
items.answer: A shadow needs a light ground to fall on. On a dark ground it simply disappears, so depth here comes from light: the open section is lit from its edge.
